title: a snapshot's self-declared worldHash switches off the contact-journal copy proof (session_snapshot_restore.ts:2058)
body:
Deferred from the 2026-08-28/29 audit fix pass. The finding was confirmed by an
adversarial verifier; it was not fixed in that pass for the reason below, which is
the fixing agent's own account after reading the code.

Needs an owner decision, and I did not want to make it by fiat. Both honest repairs are product changes: (a) verify unconditionally, which fails closed for every legitimate save whose contact prose predates the single generation covered by contact_journal_prose_migration.ts; or (b) normalize any mismatching entry to the current authored copy, which silently rewrites the player's own journal history and would make the 755-digest predecessor allowlist redundant — the conservative exact-match normalizer that exists today looks like a deliberate rejection of exactly that. Removing the laundering half (re-export stamps the current world hash over unverified prose) means the session would have to carry the snapshot's provenance hash forward instead of `indexes.worldHash`, which changes snapshot semantics for every subsequent save and is well beyond a targeted fix. My new poi/site/event/area/job proof is deliberately gated the same way (`snapshot.worldHash === worldHash`) so the contract stays consistent whichever way the owner decides; flipping both to unconditional is then a one-line change in each place.
